research_status_text: Post-earnings update (Q1 FY2027; FY2027 targets raised)
stance_text: Watch — unchanged; value slightly lower, the price fell 24%, and the rule's 15% line is still out of reach once stock compensation and the Data Center wind-down are counted
lens_text: FY2029 (June 2029) reported free cash flow x exit multiple, plus net cash, on projected diluted shares (stock compensation counted through the share count, buybacks limited to free cash flow); three-year value, undiscounted

bear.basis: Misses the FY2027 target (12%), then +4%/+3% as Data Center sales to existing customers stop in March 2028: FY2029 revenue $7,885M; FCF 20% ($1,577M) x 14x = $22.1B, plus $0.12B net cash, on 256.9M diluted shares (flat)

base.basis: Meets the 13.75% FY2027 target, then +11%/+10%: FY2029 revenue $9,128M; FCF 23% ($2,099M) x 20x = $42.0B, plus net cash, on 253.0M diluted shares (-0.5% a year)

bull.basis: Beats the target (14.5%), then +16%/+15% on Cloud and AI: FY2029 revenue $10,039M; FCF 27% ($2,710M) x 26x = $70.5B, plus net cash, on 249.2M diluted shares (-1% a year)

horizon_text: End-2029 value on FY2029 free cash flow, undiscounted
thesis: Q1 FY2027 beat its revenue target by $57M (revenue +23.7%, Cloud +30.5%, RPO +44%) and the FY2027 targets rose, yet the stock fell 16.2% the next day and is 24% below the September call. The targets imply about 9% growth for the second half, and Data Center sales to existing customers stop in March 2028. Stock compensation (24.4% of FY2026 revenue, about 19% targeted for FY2027) roughly equals free cash flow, so buybacks only offset issuance. If revenue grows about 11.6% a year to FY2029 with a 23% free-cash-flow margin at 20x, the stock is worth about $166.
consensus_view: No Street snapshot was captured. The stock peaked at $227.61 on October 23 and fell to $148.60, 22.9x trailing free cash flow and 5.0x the FY2027 revenue target, below Atlassian's own 99-month p10 of 29.5x free cash flow. The market is now pricing it near the software peer median of 21.1x despite faster growth, as if the second-half slowdown is permanent.
variant_view: The market prices Atlassian near the software peer median of 21x free cash flow, below its own p10, as if growth falls to mature-software levels. We agree growth slows, and the Data Center wind-down to March 2028 makes FY2028 the hard year, but Cloud is targeted at +26% for FY2027. The checkable test is FY2027 revenue growth of at least 14% and an initial FY2028 outlook of at least 10%; a weaker FY2028 outlook would point to the bear path.

premortem.signal: Diluted share count each quarter against 256.9 million

premortem.reason: The Watch call is wrong on the upside: AI drives a new growth leg, growth holds near 15% through FY2029, and the market pays its old 30x-plus free cash flow.

kill_criteria.condition: FY2027 revenue growth target cut to 12% or below
Initial FY2028 revenue outlook below 8% growth
FY2027 stock-based compensation above 20% of revenue (the target implies about 19%)

claims.claim: Atlassian reports Q2 FY2027 revenue of at least $1,835 million (the top of the target).
Atlassian reports FY2027 revenue growth of at least 14.0%.
Atlassian's initial FY2028 total revenue growth outlook is at least 10%.
Atlassian's FY2027 stock-based compensation is below 20% of revenue.
Atlassian's weighted-average diluted share count for Q4 FY2027 is below 256 million (the base path gives about 255.9 million).

change_my_mind: Toward Own: a price at or below about $118 with the business on the base path, or an FY2028 outlook above 13% growth
Toward Own: stock compensation falling below 16% of revenue with a falling diluted share count
Toward Avoid: the FY2027 growth target cut to 12% or below, or an FY2028 outlook below 8%
Toward Avoid: Cloud growth below 20% in any FY2027 quarter

base_rate.reference_class: US XBRL filers with $6B–$12B starting revenue, 5-year revenue CAGR, 2009–2025 (scenario rates are three-year CAGRs from FY2026 revenue of $6,572M)

notes: The September call used discounted five-year values; this update states three-year undiscounted values at the end of 2029, so the two are not directly comparable.
Fiscal years end June 30; FY2029 ends June 30, 2029.
No Street consensus snapshot was captured for this update.

Revised twice after independent review (C, then B): diluted share base, share count flat to slightly down because stock compensation roughly equals free cash flow, the March 2028 Data Center wind-down in every path, kill thresholds below the base path; see review.

First review round (C; evidence 3, valuation 2, variant view 3, risk 4, calibration 3): the share count fell 1-1.5% a year although stock compensation roughly equals free cash flow, values used basic shares, the cash decline was misattributed, and the Data Center wind-down was ignored. First draft values were $95.87 / $178.17 / $296.48, fair value $191.29.

low_score_reasons: variant_view: the market belief is inferred from a multiple with no Street data; the base case's 11% FY2028 growth sits right on the 10% test.
risk: the FY2028 kill criterion (outlook below 10%) carried the author's own 50% probability and could fire on a base-path year; the 'Toward Own near $125' trigger no longer crosses the 15% line.
review.counter_case: The call's own probabilities point lower than its weights: it gives 50% to an FY2028 outlook below 10%, a kill criterion pointing to the bear, yet weights the bear at 20%. The base returns 3.8% a year, so 39% of the fair value rests on a 91st-percentile bull. Base FY2029 FCF of $2,099M leaves about $365M after stock compensation at 19%, so 20x reported FCF is about 115x what owners keep. At 35/50/15 the value is $155.95, 1.6% a year: still Watch, but the bias should be negative.
review.response: Accepted the corrections: the Own trigger is a price at or below about $118; the FY2028 kill threshold is below 8%, under the base path, and the FY2027 target criterion fires at 12% or below so the bear path trips it; the share-count claim is below 256M, matching the base path; the bull's share decline is explained by the margin gap; the growth pillar is restated as near 10% through the wind-down. On the counter-case: a 9-10% initial FY2028 outlook is consistent with the base, because Atlassian's targets have run below results (Q1 beat the top by $57M), so the 50% claim does not imply the bear; the call shows the 35/50/15 case stays Watch. We keep a neutral bias: owner FCF after stock compensation is thin, which the low exit multiples already price, and the business met or beat every target this quarter.
